record.paper_title: A collection of open problems in celebration of Imre Leader’s 60th birthday
record.context_brief: Diamond-saturated families in the Boolean lattice
record.original_question: Let F be a family of subsets of [n] that contains no induced diamond poset, meaning there do not exist four distinct sets A, B, C, D in F with A ⊂ B ∩ C, B ∪ C ⊂ D, C not contained in B, and B not contained in C. Assume moreover that F is maximal with respect to this property, so adding any set outside F creates an induced diamond. Must every such diamond-saturated family satisfy |F| = Ω(n)?

evidence.quote: Question 7.3 (Ferrara, Kay, Kramer, Martin, Reiniger, Smith and Sullivan, [3]). Let F be a family of subsets of [n] that does not contain a diamond as an induced poset ... Assume further that F is maximal with respect to the above condition ... Is it true that |F| = Ω(n)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer and let [n] = {1, 2, …, n}. Consider the Boolean lattice 2^{[n]} consisting of all subsets of [n], ordered by inclusion. The induced diamond poset is the configuration consisting of four distinct sets A, B, C, D with A ⊂ B ∩ C, B ∪ C ⊂ D, B ⊄ C, and C ⊄ B (so that on the four elements {A,B,C,D} the only strict containments are A ⊂ B, A ⊂ C, B ⊂ D, C ⊂ D, and A ⊂ D).

Call a family F ⊆ 2^{[n]} diamond-saturated if:
(i) F contains no induced diamond, i.e. there do not exist four distinct A, B, C, D ∈ F forming an induced diamond as above; and
(ii) F is maximal with this property, i.e. for every X ∈ 2^{[n]} \ F, the family F ∪ {X} contains an induced diamond.

Let sat*(n, ◇) denote the minimum of |F| over all diamond-saturated families F ⊆ 2^{[n]}.

Question: Is it true that sat*(n, ◇) = Ω(n), i.e. that there exists a constant c > 0 such that every diamond-saturated family F ⊆ 2^{[n]} satisfies |F| ≥ c·n for all sufficiently large n?
artifact.category_tag: poset saturation in the Boolean lattice
artifact.status_search_result: The linear lower bound has been established. After progress from a logarithmic bound to a √n bound (Martin–Smith–Walker, 2020) and then to (n+1)/5 (Ivan, "The saturation number for the diamond is linear"), the exact value sat*(n, D₂) = n + 1 has subsequently been determined (Ivan–Jaffe). Thus the Ω(n) question is answered affirmatively.

status_evidence.title: The Saturation Number for the Diamond is Linear
status_evidence.snippet: Proves sat*(n, D₂) ≥ (n+1)/5, establishing a linear lower bound for the induced diamond saturation number.
status_evidence.claim: The diamond saturation number is linear in n, confirming |F| = Ω(n).

status_evidence.title: The Exact Saturation Number for the Diamond — Ivan and Jaffe
status_evidence.claim: The exact diamond saturation number is n+1, in particular Ω(n).

status_evidence.title: Minimal Diamond-Saturated Families
status_evidence.snippet: Earlier work giving a √n lower bound on the size of induced-diamond-saturated families.
status_evidence.claim: Prior to the linear bound, a √n lower bound was known.
